title: Lakshmana's warning
hook: the path Vali took is not closed
carry: the path Vali took is not closed

segments.voice: Yesterday: the rains ended, and Hanuman reminded Sugriva early and gently: don't wait to be asked.

No messenger. Not yesterday, not today. Rama looks down the mountain toward the city where his friend is enjoying a throne Rama won for him. He doesn't know about Hanuman's reminder or the orders that went out. All he sees is a clear road and a silent city. His patience, which has held through grief and rain, finally gives way. Valmiki lets us hear all of it.
screen: `NO MESSENGER.` → `A SILENT CITY BELOW.` → `PATIENCE GIVES WAY.`

segments.voice: Rama speaks to Lakshmana, first in grief, then in anger. The time we agreed on is here, he says, and Sugriva hasn't come. He's drunk on his good fortune. He thinks I'm weak, a man without a kingdom, someone he can forget. So Rama gives Lakshmana a message to carry, and it isn't subtle. Tell him: the path Vali took is not closed. Keep your word, or follow Vali. It's a hard line. A friendship sworn before fire has weight when it's broken. Rama gave first, at real cost, and he expects faith kept. Notice he doesn't ask for gratitude. He asks for the promise. Then watch Lakshmana. Rama is angry; Lakshmana is angrier. He wants to go down and kill Sugriva today. So Rama, even while sending him, has to calm his brother: don't kill him. Speak gently first. Remind him of the friendship. Usually it's Lakshmana who calms Rama; now the brothers have swapped places. The word that matters here is samaya, an agreement, and also an appointed time. In Sanskrit it can mean both. Rama's complaint isn't that Sugriva enjoyed himself after years of exile. It's that he let the agreed time slip by. A promise has a when as well as a what. Lakshmana picks up his bow and walks down the mountain toward Kishkindha.
screen: `RAMA'S GRIEF TURNS TO ANGER.` · `THE PATH VALI TOOK IS NOT CLOSED.` · `SPEAK GENTLY FIRST.` · `SAMAYA: AGREEMENT AND TIME.`

segments.voice: Think of one promise with a date on it: a visit, a deadline, a reply you said you'd send. Breathe in and feel where it sits in time, near or far; breathe out and let your body relax around it. You don't have to act on it now; just know when it is.
Lakshmana's warning. Rama's message: the path Vali took is not closed. Keep the agreed time.
Your line: the path Vali took is not closed. Even Rama's patience has an end. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Storytellers use Rama's message to Sugriva, the path Vali took is not closed, to talk about keeping one's word to a friend.

fork.setup: you're Rama. autumn is here and Sugriva hasn't come. what do you do?
options: send Lakshmana with a hard message, but tell him to speak gently first.
fork.reveal: Rama sends the warning, the path Vali took is not closed, and restrains his angrier brother.

original.note: Sanskrit samaya: an agreement or compact, and also an appointed time.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama threatens Sugriva in a rage.
what it means: he sends a hard warning about broken time, and restrains Lakshmana.
what a scholar hears: Kishkindha 30 has Rama's message (the path by which Vali went is not closed); the counsel to speak gently opens Kishkindha 31.
recall: Sita's father, keeper of Shiva's bow

chat.says: Why was Rama so angry at Sugriva? Wasn't he just enjoying his new kingdom?
options: The agreed time had passed. Rama didn't ask for thanks; he asked for the promise.
Rama was jealous that Sugriva had a palace while he lived in a cave.
Rama had learned that Sugriva was secretly siding with Ravana against him.
chat.meaning: Rama's complaint is samaya, an agreement with a time attached: Sugriva let the agreed time slip. Rama asks for the promise, not gratitude.

samaya.meaning: an agreement, and also an appointed time

Vali.meaning: Sugriva's elder brother, once king of Kishkindha

Sugriva.meaning: the monkey king, Vali's younger brother, Rama's ally

Lakshmana.meaning: Rama's younger brother, beside him in exile
